summary:
A space telescope has helped scientists read a very old message carried by light. Three distant galaxies were already sending carbon, oxygen and other elements into nearby space when the universe was about 500 million years old.

The study appeared on September 24. ScienceDaily featured it on October 2. The galaxies did not change this week: their light has taken more than 13 billion years to reach us.

Researchers used observations from the James Webb Space Telescope. As a galaxy's light passes through gas, some colors are absorbed. The missing colors help identify what the gas contains. Changes in those patterns also showed gas moving out of the galaxies.

The early universe mostly contained hydrogen and helium. Stars made heavier elements, including carbon and oxygen. When stars released material, those elements could spread and later become part of other stars and planets.

The finding helps scientists investigate how the universe changed. It does not show that life existed in these galaxies. Instead, it reveals that some important ingredients were already traveling through space surprisingly early.
title: Early Galaxies Shared Their Elements
why_it_matters: The study helps explain how matter became available for later stars and planets.
